meta.title: Retirement Simulator — Monte Carlo Retirement Planning
meta.description: Stress-test your retirement plan against thousands of simulated market futures. Free, private, and computed in your browser.

hero.badge: Monte Carlo engine · runs in your browser
hero.subtitle: The engine replays your whole financial life through thousands of simulated markets — volatility, inflation, pension, and spending — so you see the full range of outcomes before you bet your retirement on a single guess.
hero.note: No sign-up needed. Without signing in, your plan data never leaves this browser — only page views are counted. If you sign in, your plans are stored in your account.
hero.lede: One average return tells you nothing.
hero.runsNote: The chart above is one baked run of the engine: {previewRuns} paths, {previewRate} of them still funded at the end. The same plan on your own dashboard runs {defaultRuns} paths by default and reports {defaultRate} — fewer samples, same plan. Raise the run count in the plan editor whenever you want a tighter answer.

features.title: Everything a serious plan needs
features.subtitle: A complete planning engine — no spreadsheet gymnastics required.

monteCarlo.title: A real Monte Carlo engine
monteCarlo.body: Lognormal returns sampled with the Box–Muller transform — thousands of complete market lifetimes, computed in seconds.

live.title: Instant what-if answers
live.body: Move any slider and the percentiles redraw in about 100 milliseconds. Interrogate every assumption, live.

phases.title: Both halves of the journey
phases.body: Accumulation to drawdown in one model: savings growth, statutory pension, one-time windfalls, and custom expense streams.

reports.title: Reports worth sharing
reports.body: Export a clean, comprehensive PDF of your plan — assumptions, charts, and recommendations included.

privacy.title: Private by design
privacy.body: No account needed and no tracking of your finances: the simulation and the PDF report are computed in your browser, and your inputs stay in its local storage. Only page views are counted. If you sign in, your plans are also stored in your account.

bilingual.title: Bilingual & localized
bilingual.body: Full English and German interfaces with proper currency, number, and date formatting throughout.

how.title: From guess to plan in five minutes

step1.title: Describe your plan
step1.body: Ages, assets, savings, pension, and spending — a guided setup that takes about five minutes.

step2.title: Run thousands of futures
step2.body: The engine replays your entire financial life through simulated markets — good decades and bad.

step3.title: Stress-test and refine
step3.body: Tune assumptions live, watch the bands respond, and export the PDF once the plan holds.

cta.title: Know where you stand.

capitalGainsTax.label: Abgeltungsteuer (capital gains tax)
capitalGainsTax.tooltip: German flat tax on realised investment gains, including solidarity surcharge — 26.375% for most savers. Only the gains portion of a sale is taxed.

averageROI.label: Average ROI
averageROI.tooltip: Expected annual return on investments. Historical stock market: ~7-10%. Bond portfolio: ~3-5%. Diversified portfolio: ~6-8%.

roiVolatility.label: ROI Volatility
roiVolatility.tooltip: Standard deviation of returns. Higher volatility means more uncertainty. Conservative: 5-10%, Moderate: 10-15%, Aggressive: 15-25%.

averageInflation.label: Average Inflation
averageInflation.tooltip: Expected annual inflation rate. ECB target: 2%. Historical average in developed countries: 2-3%.

inflationVolatility.label: Inflation Volatility
inflationVolatility.tooltip: How much inflation varies year-to-year. Historical range: 0.5-1.5%. Higher volatility creates more uncertainty in retirement costs.

simulationRuns.label: Number of Runs
simulationRuns.tooltip: More paths narrow the sampling interval and take longer to calculate. The market assumptions stay the same.

withdrawalStrategy.label: Withdrawal Strategy
withdrawalStrategy.tooltip: Four rules for turning a portfolio into an income. They trade spending stability against the chance of running out — the planner below shows both.

fixedReal.label: Fixed real spending
fixedReal.description: Spend the same purchasing power every year — steady income, highest risk of running dry.

vanguardDynamic.label: Dynamic with guardrails (Vanguard)
vanguardDynamic.description: Follow the portfolio, but never cut below the floor or raise above the ceiling.

guytonKlinger.label: Guyton-Klinger guardrails
guytonKlinger.description: Inflation raises as usual, plus a 10% cut or raise once the withdrawal rate drifts 20% off course.

percentOfPortfolio.label: Percent of portfolio
percentOfPortfolio.description: Take a fixed share of the portfolio each year, on top of pensions and other income. The rule alone never empties the portfolio — scheduled expenses or a spending floor can — and income swings with the market.

dsWithdrawalRate.label: Withdrawal rate
dsWithdrawalRate.tooltip: The share of the portfolio the rule takes each year, on top of pensions and recurring income. Vanguard: the rate targeted each year. Guyton-Klinger: the rate the guardrails are measured against. Percent of portfolio: the rate taken outright.

dsCeilingRate.label: Spending ceiling
dsCeilingRate.tooltip: Largest raise versus last year’s inflation-adjusted spending.

dsFloorRate.label: Spending floor
dsFloorRate.tooltip: Largest cut versus last year’s inflation-adjusted spending.

monteCarlo.label: Monte Carlo
monteCarlo.description: Random draws from your return, volatility and inflation assumptions.

assetTable.caption: Portfolio value milestones by age and percentile

aria.brush: Age range shown, {startAge} to {endAge}. Drag the handles to zoom the chart into part of the timeline.

explanation.reading: The solid line is the median monthly spending that was actually paid (the rule plus scheduled items); the shaded band spans the 10th to 90th percentile. Once a path’s portfolio is used up it shows only what pensions and income still cover. Hover any age to see the rule’s withdrawal rate: the part of regular spending the portfolio pays, divided by the portfolio value the rule measures — before capital gains tax and without scheduled items.

strategies.fixedReal: Fixed real spending keeps the planned budget on an inflation path. Portfolio returns decide whether the portfolio lasts, but they never change the budget the plan asks for.
strategies.vanguardDynamic: The Vanguard guardrails start from the planned first retirement-year budget. After that, what counts as affordable is pensions and recurring income plus {withdrawalRate} of the prior year-end portfolio — capped at {ceiling} above and {floor} below last year’s inflation-adjusted spending. Spending is not cut below what pensions and income cover anyway.
strategies.guytonKlinger: Guyton-Klinger keeps the planned budget on an inflation path and watches the portfolio’s withdrawal rate: the part of spending that pensions and income do not cover, divided by the portfolio value. It cuts 10% whenever that rate runs more than 20% above {withdrawalRate}, and adds 10% whenever it runs more than 20% below. Spending is not cut below what pensions and income cover anyway.
strategies.percentOfPortfolio: Percent of portfolio takes {withdrawalRate} of the prior year-end portfolio every year, on top of pensions and recurring income. Spending follows the market in both directions; only an explicit floor puts a bottom under it.

legend.note: Spending shows what was actually paid. The tooltip withdrawal rate is the rate the rule works with: the portfolio’s share of regular spending divided by the portfolio value, as a ratio of means. Tax on sales and scheduled items come on top.

withdrawalPlanner.saleMethod: The model allocates the same share of the portfolio’s purchase cost to each euro sold. It applies the selected partial exemption and remaining annual allowance to gains. Individual purchase lots (FIFO) and loss carryforwards are outside the model.
withdrawalPlanner.noParams: This strategy has no settings: it simply spends the plan’s budget, inflation-linked.

cashflowResults.method: Averages of the actual cash flows across all simulated paths. These figures add up; they are not the median (P50) used in the charts. Rounded amounts may differ by a euro.
cashflowResults.missing: Recalculate the simulation to see the annual cash-flow breakdown.
cashflowResults.incomeTax: Tax on pensions and other income
cashflowResults.totalTax: Total taxes deducted in this year: {amount}. These are already included in the calculation.
cashflowResults.shortfallNote: Some simulated paths cannot fund the full budget. The unfunded amount is not available to spend.
cashflowResults.workingYears: Before retirement, salary is assumed to cover ordinary living costs. Only the savings contribution and additional scheduled cash flows move the portfolio.
cashflowResults.tableNote: Annual averages; taxes are already deducted from income and gross withdrawals. Do not subtract them again.
cashflowResults.assumptions: Income-tax treatment follows each item’s settings (2026 tariff for ordinary and one-fifth-rule income). Pension tax uses the configured effective rate on its taxable portion. Capital gains tax applies to realised gains after the selected allowance and fund exemption. This is a planning approximation: wages beyond the savings contribution, deductions, church tax and the income-tax solidarity surcharge are not modelled.
cashflowResults.legacyOneOffTiming: This plan credits one-off income at the end of the entered year. The table shows it with its tax at the next age, or at the close of the final year.
cashflowResults.oneOffTiming: One-off income is available at the start of the entered age. The table shows the credit and its tax in that year.

agePlanner.title: When can I retire?
agePlanner.intro: Compare retirement ages for a steady monthly budget in today’s euros. Each additional working year adds savings and shortens retirement.
agePlanner.error: The comparison could not run. Try again.
agePlanner.none: No age from {from} to {to} meets your target.
agePlanner.gain: Gain vs. retiring a year earlier
agePlanner.sample: The affordable budget is the highest €10 step reaching {probability} success through age {end}, inclusive.
agePlanner.budgetMethod: From retirement, your target replaces ordinary lifetime expenses and stays constant in purchasing power — this table always tests fixed inflation-adjusted withdrawals, even if your plan uses a dynamic withdrawal rule. Scheduled expenses are added on their original dates. Pensions, other income, taxes, savings and any bequest goal follow your plan.
agePlanner.successMethod: An age qualifies when enough paths fund at least 99% of the requested spending every year and meet any bequest goal. The comparison tests every age from your current age to the latest age selected. The detailed calculation includes the quick sample and adds paths. The interval measures sampling uncertainty under the selected assumptions.
agePlanner.quickSample: Quick comparison on {paths, number} shared market paths.
agePlanner.finalSample: Detailed comparison on {paths, number} shared market paths.
agePlanner.historicalSample: Comparison across all {paths, number} historical start years.
agePlanner.interval: At age {age}, the 95% Monte Carlo interval for success at the target budget is {low}–{high}.

shortfalls.title: Explore spending shortfalls
shortfalls.fundingCount: Funding gaps in {count, number} of {total, number} paths
shortfalls.fundingDefinition: A path has a funding gap when more than 1% of a year’s requested spending goes unpaid. This includes expenses before retirement.
shortfalls.atHorizon: At age {age}, {count, number} of the {affected, number} affected paths still had a gap. The simulation ends at that age.
shortfalls.bequest: In {count, number} of {total, number} paths, spending was funded in every year but the final balance fell short of the {target} bequest goal in today’s euros.
shortfalls.lifestyleFunded: Of these paths, {count, number} funded the planned spending in every year.
shortfalls.lifestyleCount: In {count, number} of {total, number} paths, funded everyday spending fell below your {target} monthly minimum in today’s euros after allowing for scheduled expenses.
shortfalls.noFloor: Set a personal monthly minimum to see how often your withdrawal rule leaves less for everyday spending, even when all payments are funded.
shortfalls.method: Figures are medians across the paths affected by each type of gap. Each path contributes its average monthly gap during affected years. Years with a gap can be separated by fully funded years.
